info.title: Pyas API
info.description:
One API for Google Calendar, Microsoft Outlook, Zoom and virtual calendars. Every request must include an `x-api-key` header. Test keys (`pyas_sk_test_`) work only in the sandbox.

## Test requests in your sandbox

You can send any request to your sandbox from the API reference in the docs. When you're signed in to the dashboard, each operation's **Try it** button sends the request with a key created for you. That key works only in your sandbox, so your live data is never affected.

Placeholders in double braces, such as `{{account.avery}}` or `{{event.avery.design}}`, stand for the people, calendars and events in your sandbox. `{{in.1d.14:00}}` stands for tomorrow at 14:00 UTC. When you're signed in, the placeholders are replaced with your sandbox's own values.

In addition to its virtual accounts, the sandbox includes simulated Google, Microsoft Outlook and Zoom accounts: `{{account.google}}` (Avery), `{{account.outlook}}` (Sam) and `{{account.zoom}}` (Avery). They respond as those providers do, with the same features and the same errors, but never contact the providers. Google Meet and Microsoft Teams links, Zoom meetings, sharing roles, labels and categories, calendar groups, invitations to respond to, files, reminders and working locations all work in the sandbox. In a sandbox, Google and Outlook accounts are always simulated.

## Scenarios

### Find a time when two people are free and book it

Find meeting times across both calendars, then create an event in the first free slot and invite the other person.

1. Find 30-minute slots in the next week: `POST /v2/meeting-times`

```json
{
  "accountIds": [
    "{{account.avery}}",
    "{{account.sam}}"
  ],
  "from": "{{in.1d}}",
  "to": "{{in.8d}}",
  "durationMinutes": 30,
  "timezone": "America/New_York"
}
```

   Save `data.0.startsAt` as `{{slot.startsAt}}`, `data.0.endsAt` as `{{slot.endsAt}}`.

2. Book the first slot: `POST /v2/events`

```json
{
  "accountId": "{{account.avery}}",
  "title": "Catch-up with Sam",
  "startsAt": "{{slot.startsAt}}",
  "endsAt": "{{slot.endsAt}}",
  "attendees": [
    {
      "email": "sam@example.com",
      "name": "Sam Patel"
    }
  ]
}
```

   Save `data.id` as `{{booked.id}}`.

3. Retrieve the event: `GET /v2/events/{{booked.id}}?accountId={{account.avery}}`

### Move one occurrence of a recurring meeting

Create a weekly meeting, list its occurrences, and move one of them without changing the rest.

1. Create a weekly meeting: `POST /v2/events`

```json
{
  "accountId": "{{account.avery}}",
  "title": "Weekly review",
  "startsAt": "{{in.1d.15:00}}",
  "endsAt": "{{in.1d.15:30}}",
  "recurrence": "FREQ=WEEKLY;COUNT=6"
}
```

   Save `data.id` as `{{series.id}}`.

2. List its occurrences for the next 3 weeks: `GET /v2/events/{{series.id}}/instances?accountId={{account.avery}}&from={{in.0d}}&to={{in.21d}}`

   Save `data.1.id` as `{{occurrence.id}}`.

3. Move the second occurrence 1 hour later: `PATCH /v2/events/{{occurrence.id}}?accountId={{account.avery}}`

```json
{
  "startsAt": "{{in.8d.16:00}}",
  "endsAt": "{{in.8d.16:30}}"
}
```

### Store your own data on events and search by it

Pyas stores your metadata with the event on every provider, and you can search events by their metadata.

1. Create an event with your deal ID: `POST /v2/events`

```json
{
  "accountId": "{{account.avery}}",
  "title": "Pricing call",
  "startsAt": "{{in.4d.16:00}}",
  "endsAt": "{{in.4d.16:30}}",
  "metadata": {
    "dealId": "deal_1007",
    "stage": "proposal"
  }
}
```

2. Find the event by its deal ID: `GET /v2/events?metadata.dealId=deal_1007`

### Keep a copy in sync by reading only changes

Start a sync of a time window, save the `syncToken`, create an event, and then read only that change.

1. Start a sync of the next month: `GET /v2/events?accountId={{account.avery}}&from={{in.0d}}&to={{in.30d}}&sync=true&limit=250`

   Save `meta.syncToken` as `{{sync.token}}`.

2. Create an event: `POST /v2/events`

```json
{
  "accountId": "{{account.avery}}",
  "title": "New this afternoon",
  "startsAt": "{{in.1d.19:00}}",
  "endsAt": "{{in.1d.19:30}}"
}
```

3. Read only the changes: `GET /v2/events?accountId={{account.avery}}&syncToken={{sync.token}}`

### Publish a calendar people can subscribe to

Publish a virtual calendar as an iCalendar feed that shows only busy times, then get its link.

1. Enable the feed, showing only busy times: `PUT /v2/calendars/primary/feed?accountId={{account.yuki}}`

```json
{
  "details": "busy"
}
```

2. Get the feed link: `GET /v2/calendars/primary/feed?accountId={{account.yuki}}`

### Attach a document to an event

Attach a link to an event, list the attachments, and delete the link.

1. Attach the agenda: `POST /v2/events/{{event.yuki.design}}/attachments?accountId={{account.yuki}}`

```json
{
  "url": "https://example.com/design-agenda.pdf",
  "name": "Design agenda.pdf"
}
```

   Save `data.id` as `{{attachment.id}}`.

2. List the attachments: `GET /v2/events/{{event.yuki.design}}/attachments?accountId={{account.yuki}}`

3. Delete the attachment: `DELETE /v2/events/{{event.yuki.design}}/attachments/{{attachment.id}}?accountId={{account.yuki}}`

### Add a Google Meet, Microsoft Teams or Zoom link with meeting settings

Each calendar provider creates its own meetings, Google Meet on Google and Microsoft Teams on Outlook. A Zoom account adds Zoom meetings to any calendar. Meeting settings use one set of options for all three services. A setting that a service doesn't support is rejected, and you can read the settings back after you write them.

1. Create a Google event with a Meet link that only invited people can join without asking: `POST /v2/events`

```json
{
  "accountId": "{{account.google}}",
  "title": "Design critique",
  "startsAt": "{{in.2d.16:00}}",
  "endsAt": "{{in.2d.17:00}}",
  "conferencing": {
    "provider": "meet",
    "options": {
      "admission": "invited",
      "recording": "cloud"
    }
  }
}
```

   Save `data.id` as `{{meet.id}}`.

2. Read the meeting settings back: `GET /v2/events/{{meet.id}}?accountId={{account.google}}&include=conferencingSettings`

3. Create an Outlook event with a Teams meeting where everyone waits in the lobby: `POST /v2/events`

```json
{
  "accountId": "{{account.outlook}}",
  "title": "Supplier call",
  "startsAt": "{{in.3d.10:00}}",
  "endsAt": "{{in.3d.10:30}}",
  "conferencing": {
    "provider": "teams",
    "options": {
      "admission": "organizer"
    }
  }
}
```

4. Create a Zoom meeting on a virtual calendar with the Zoom account: `POST /v2/events`

```json
{
  "accountId": "{{account.avery}}",
  "title": "Customer onboarding",
  "startsAt": "{{in.4d.15:00}}",
  "endsAt": "{{in.4d.16:00}}",
  "conferencing": {
    "provider": "zoom",
    "accountId": "{{account.zoom}}",
    "options": {
      "admission": "organizer",
      "muteOnEntry": true
    }
  }
}
```

   Save `data.id` as `{{zoom.id}}`.

5. Reschedule the event and its Zoom meeting: `PATCH /v2/events/{{zoom.id}}?accountId={{account.avery}}`

```json
{
  "startsAt": "{{in.5d.15:00}}",
  "endsAt": "{{in.5d.16:00}}"
}
```

### Respond to an invitation and propose another time

Respond tentatively to an invitation from someone else on an Outlook calendar and propose a new time. On Google, the response is recorded without a proposed time.

1. Read the invitation: `GET /v2/events/{{event.outlook.invite}}?accountId={{account.outlook}}`

2. Respond tentatively and propose a time 1 hour later: `POST /v2/events/{{event.outlook.invite}}/respond?accountId={{account.outlook}}`

```json
{
  "response": "tentative",
  "comment": "Could we start an hour later?",
  "proposedTime": {
    "startsAt": "{{in.2d.16:00}}",
    "endsAt": "{{in.2d.17:00}}"
  }
}
```

3. Accept an invitation on Google: `POST /v2/events/{{event.google.invite}}/respond?accountId={{account.google}}`

```json
{
  "response": "accepted"
}
```

### Import data another app stored on events

Read the extended properties another app wrote on Google events, preview what an import would copy, then copy them into metadata.

1. Read the extended properties on an event: `GET /v2/events/{{event.google.trip}}?accountId={{account.google}}&include=extendedProperties`

2. Preview what an import would copy: `POST /v2/metadata/import`

```json
{
  "accountIds": [
    "{{account.google}}"
  ],
  "dryRun": true
}
```

3. Copy them into metadata: `POST /v2/metadata/import`

```json
{
  "accountIds": [
    "{{account.google}}"
  ]
}
```

   Save `data.importId` as `{{import.id}}`.

4. Check the import's progress: `GET /v2/metadata/imports/{{import.id}}`

### Test webhooks before you write a handler

Every sandbox has an inbox, hosted by Pyas, that receives every sandbox event. Send it sample events and see exactly what arrives and how it is signed. Then point a test endpoint of your own at your handler.

1. Send a sample event.updated delivery, signed like a real one: `POST /v2/webhooks/{{webhook.inbox}}/test`

```json
{
  "type": "event.updated"
}
```

2. List the deliveries and their attempts: `GET /v2/webhooks/deliveries?webhookId={{webhook.inbox}}`

3. Retrieve the signing secret: `GET /v2/webhooks/{{webhook.inbox}}/secret`

4. List every event type with a sample: `GET /v2/webhooks/event-types`

delete.description:
Deletes an account from your app and sends a `connection.deleted` webhook.

For a Google, Outlook or Zoom account, Pyas deletes the credentials it stores for the account and stops watching it for changes. The user's calendars at the provider are not changed, and the user can connect the account again later. With a live key, the account no longer counts toward your plan.

A virtual account is deleted with all of its calendars and events.

For every account, the metadata you stored on its events and calendars is deleted too. In the sandbox, resetting the sandbox restores deleted accounts.

**In the sandbox:** This example deletes the simulated Google account in the sandbox. Virtual accounts are deleted the same way. Resetting the sandbox with `POST /v2/sandbox/reset` restores deleted sandbox accounts.

get.description:
Returns the status of each account. `overall.status` is `healthy`, `attention` or `broken`, and `overall` includes the reason and the fix. The response also shows which features are available, and includes a message for the account's owner when they need to take action. `meta.needsAttention` is the number of accounts in the response whose `overall.status` is not `healthy`.

get.description:
Lists the events in one calendar of a connected account, within an optional time window and with optional filters.

To list several accounts as one timeline in start order, send `accountIds` or `subjectId` with `from` and `to`. To find events by your own metadata across the app, send up to 5 `metadata.<key>=<value>` parameters.

A recurring series is returned as one event unless `expand=true`. `sync=true` starts an incremental sync of the window. To get only the changes since then, send the `syncToken` from the last page in a later request.

The v1 parameter names (`calendarId`, `timeMin`, `timeMax`, `maxResults`, `nextPageToken` and others) still work. Responses to requests that use them include a `Pyas-Deprecated-Fields` header.

refuse.iCalUID: retrieve the event by its ID instead.
refuse.$filter: v2 does not pass Outlook query filters through. Use v2's own filters, and read extended properties with include=extendedProperties and extendedPropertyIds.
refuse.$expand: read extended properties with include=extendedProperties and extendedPropertyIds, or the provider's whole event with include=raw.

notes: A `maxResults` above 250 is capped. The remaining events are returned on the next page.
`orderBy=updated` maps to `sort=updated`. `orderBy=startTime` is the order of an expanded window (`expand=true`).
`showDeleted=true` also returns cancelled events. On an incremental sync, deleted events are listed in `meta.deletedIds`.
For `calendarView`, send `from`, `to` and `expand=true`. This returns the window with recurring series expanded.
`privateExtendedProperty` and `sharedExtendedProperty` (`key=value`, repeatable) still search Google events by extended property, to help you move. Search by `metadata.<key>` instead.
Outlook's `$filter` and `$expand` are refused. Use v2's own filters, and read extended properties with `include=extendedProperties` and `extendedPropertyIds`.

post.description:
Creates a new key with the same name, scopes and mode, and returns its value once in this response. A key can rotate only itself, so send this request with the key that you want to rotate, and use `current` as the key ID. To rotate a different key, use the dashboard. The old key gets a grace period during which both keys work (default 24 hours, at most 168), so you can deploy the new key without any failed requests. When the grace period ends, the old key stops working. Pyas sends an `api_key.expiring` webhook 1 hour before the grace period ends, and an `api_key.revoked` webhook when it ends. A key can be rotated only once.

**In the sandbox:** Rotates the key that sent the request. The API reference sends requests with a key created for the docs, which can't be rotated. With your own key, the response includes the new key (returned only once), and the old key keeps working for 24 more hours.

status.description: The delivery status: `queued`, `sent`, `captured` (in the sandbox, never sent), `held` (over the daily limit), `suppressed` (the address bounced or complained before) or `failed`.

ics.description: The iCalendar text sent to the attendee. In the sandbox, the text that would have been sent.

status.description: `rotating` means the key has been replaced but keeps working until `graceEndsAt`.

last4.description: The last 4 characters of the key, to help you tell keys apart.

seenInBrowser.description: When the key was last sent from a web page, and from which origin. A live key sent that way is refused (`AUTH_KEY_IN_BROWSER`); a test key still works, with a `Pyas-Warning` header. Keys belong in server code.

keyId.description: The API key that made the request.

kind.description: `mcp`: an AI tool connected to the Pyas MCP server. `cli`: the Pyas CLI. `package`: one of the Pyas packages your code runs, such as `@pyas/ai-tools`.

name.description: The name the tool registered with, such as "Claude", "Cursor" or "Pyas CLI", or the name of the package.

client.description: The tool or Pyas package that made the request, or `null` for your own code.

route.description: The endpoint, with IDs replaced by `:id`, such as "GET /v2/events/:id".

operationId.description: The operation in the API reference, such as `events.create`.

error.description: The error returned for the request, if it failed, with a link to the error's documentation.

replayed.description: `true` if the response was replayed from an earlier request with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

cache.description: Where read data was served from, as reported in the `X-Pyas-Cache` header: `HIT`, `MISS`, `PARTIAL`, `BYPASS` or `STALE`.

queuedMs.description: The longest time, in milliseconds, that a provider request waited in the queue, as reported in the `X-Pyas-Provider-Queued-Ms` header.

provider.description: `google`, `microsoft`, `pyas` (virtual) or `zoom`. For the sandbox's simulated Google and Outlook accounts, the value includes "(simulated)".

operation.description: The operation Pyas performed for the request, such as `listEvents`, `createEvent` or `getFreeBusy`.

error.description: The error code, if the operation failed.

path.description: The provider path, with IDs, email addresses and tokens replaced by `:id`.

status.description: The HTTP status the provider returned, or `null` if no response was received.

failure.description: `timeout` or `network` when no response was received.

retryAfter.description: The number of seconds the provider asked Pyas to wait before retrying, when it throttled the request.

providerCalls.description: Each HTTP request made to Google, Microsoft or Zoom. Requests for sandbox accounts don't make any.

webhookEvents.description: The webhook events the request triggered. Retrieve an event with GET /v2/webhooks/events/{eventId}, and its deliveries with GET /v2/webhooks/deliveries?eventId={eventId}.

invitations.description: The invitations the request sent. Retrieve one with GET /v2/invitations/{invitationId}.

omitted.description: The number of entries omitted because a list exceeded its limit of 50 entries.

optionalFree.description: Optional attendees free for the whole slot.

rooms.description: Rooms free for the whole slot, when the request includes `rooms`.

id.description: The meeting ID at the provider: Zoom's meeting number, or Microsoft Teams' online meeting ID.

provider.description: The meeting service: `zoom`, `teams` or `meet`, as in `conferencing.provider` on events. The response's top-level `provider` is the account's: `zoom`, `microsoft` or `google`.

kind.description: `recurring` repeats at fixed times (`recurrence`). `recurringNoFixedTime` (Zoom) and `space` (a Google Meet link) work at any time.

title.description: `null` for a Google Meet link, which has no title.

startsAt.description: For a recurring meeting, its first occurrence.

occurrences.description: A recurring meeting's occurrences, from a get. Empty in a list.

Meeting.description: A meeting on its own, with no calendar event. To add a meeting to an event, use `conferencing` on the event instead.

accountId.description: The `accountId` of a connected Zoom account, a Microsoft work or school account for Microsoft Teams, or a Google account for a Google Meet link.

title.description: The meeting's topic. Required for Zoom and Microsoft Teams; a Google Meet link has none.

startsAt.description: When it starts (ISO 8601). For a recurring meeting, its first occurrence. Required for Zoom and Microsoft Teams; a Google Meet link works at any time.

durationMinutes.description: Its length in minutes. 30 if you don't set it.

timezone.description: An IANA time zone, such as `America/New_York`. Recurring meetings repeat in it.

recurrence.description: Zoom only. A recurrence rule (RRULE): FREQ=DAILY, WEEKLY or MONTHLY, INTERVAL, BYDAY or BYMONTHDAY, and COUNT (up to 60) or UNTIL. Zoom needs an end.

attendees.description: People invited by email. On Microsoft Teams, the meeting's attendees.

recurrence.description: A recurrence rule (RRULE): FREQ=DAILY, WEEKLY or MONTHLY, INTERVAL, BYDAY or BYMONTHDAY, and COUNT (up to 60) or UNTIL. Zoom needs an end. `null` makes it a single meeting.

MeetingPatch.description: Only the fields you send change.

scopes.description: The Google scopes the key was found in.

conflicts.description: On how many events the key held different values in private and shared. The private value is imported.

skippedKeys.description: Provider keys that can't be used as metadata keys.

skipped.description: The first events that were skipped, with the reason for each.

accessible.description: Reported by Outlook. `null` on Google Calendar.

seededAt.description: When the sandbox was last populated with sample data.

examples.description: The IDs in this sandbox that the examples in the API reference use, such as {{account.avery}}, {{calendar.avery.work}} and {{event.avery.design}}.

test.description: Requests made with test keys, in the v2 sandbox.

v2Share.description: The share of live requests made to v2, from 0 to 1. `null` when there were no live requests.

test.description: Requests made with test keys, in the v2 sandbox.

endpoint.description: The method and path, such as `GET /v2/events`.

mode.description: `test` endpoints receive events from the sandbox.

payloadVersion.description: With `v1`, the endpoint receives v1 deliveries, as it did before v2. With `v2`, it receives signed v2 deliveries of the types in `events`, which are retried and recorded.

events.description: The v2 event types the endpoint receives, or `*` for all types.

triggers.description: The v1 triggers the endpoint receives. Used only with v1 payloads.

name.description: The name of the header the credential is sent in, when `type` is `header`.

auth.description: The credential Pyas sends to your endpoint with each delivery, if any. Its value is never returned.

signingSecret.description: Set for endpoints with v2 payloads. To retrieve the full secret, call `GET /v2/webhooks/:webhookId/secret`.

consecutiveFailures.description: The number of consecutive deliveries that failed after every attempt. The endpoint is disabled after 50 consecutive failed deliveries.

responseBody.description: The first 1 KB of the response body.
